doc.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024

title: Never playing for dancers; all he wanted was the piano
summary: As a young hippie jazz kid he never played for dancers and only wanted to play piano, which still moves him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: That’s pretty profound. Thank you for that. I’m envious on a couple levels but one is that you’ve written for the dance. And I wonder if in your career before those commissions, if you ever were a dance — a pianist for a dance company, just accompanying their workouts and providing music for them to move to?

We were a little stoned out, like little stoned hippie jazz kids. We didn’t play for dancers, we just sat around looking cool, playing little dives and thinking we were the cat’s ass. I mean you know I didn’t know even dance existed. I didn’t know anything existed. In fact I had — I ran into an old girlfriend who said, “Man, what’s your problem? All the girls wanted to date you and all you wanted to do was play the piano.” I said, “If I had known that things might have turned out differently. Nonetheless —”
You said that before we started recording today, looking at all the boxes behind you, you said, “All I wanted to do was play the piano.”

All — that’s all I wanted to do. And I wasn’t just posing. I genuinely love this instrument. I — to this day I get up and I look at that instrument and I’m filled with emotion. That’s the privilege, the privilege of being an instrumentalist, a composer and educator. It does not fail to break my heart every day, what a beautiful and loving obligation that is that I have.
